about: The thresholds the outreach recipes hold candidates to, as requests to tool:classify-a-record (tools/formulas do-work/classify-by-rules.mjs, the Workshop's one rule owner), never a rule language of their own. A row's `facts` say what is read from a candidate record; each of its `keep` rules must hold for the candidate to stay; each `signals` entry is one rule with its weight: a candidate is classified once per signal with rules: [that rule], its signals are the keys that came back and its score is their weights added. `prepare` says, in words, any number the step works out from the candidate's own lists before it is classified (a count of reviews, a share), so the rule reads a plain number. A person's own row (the recipe's input source_row) has the same shape and replaces the shipped one; every number here is a default, not a law. Moved out of tools/find-signals-of-need/sources.json (2026-11-02) when that finder was deleted.

records.label: Companies whose job post has stayed open
records.meaning: A role that has stayed open for weeks at a small company shows a problem it has not solved inside, and budget set aside for it. The post's own list of day-to-day duties says what is broken.

keep.label: Open 21 days or more at a company of 10 to 200 people

rule.label: The post has been open for 30 days or more.
The post has been open for 21 days or more.

records.label: Local businesses in a place, scored by what their reviews say
records.meaning: A business whose customers keep naming one delay, or whose reviews suddenly pick up, has told you what it needs. Candidates for a place come from the person's map data connection.

prepare.says: How many of its reviews mention any of these words, ignoring capitals
How many of its dated reviews fall in the last 90 days
Its dated reviews in the last 90 days divided by all its dated reviews

rule.label: A large share of the reviews are from the last 90 days.
At least 5 reviews came in during the last 90 days.

records.label: Vendors in a category, scored only on proof they publish
records.meaning: A 'best X for Y' comparison earns citations when every score can be checked. Each metric is a number someone can verify at a public address; a metric with no proof address is sent as null, which a rule reads as nothing proven, so it never fires a signal. A sponsored vendor is scored by the same row as everyone else: sponsorship is a label on the page, never a fact here.

rule.label: At least 5 customers are named in public case studies.
At least 100 public reviews on an independent review site.
Rated 4.5 or more out of 5 on that review site.
Its public status page shows 99.9% uptime or more over the last 90 days.
Its price is published on its own site, no sales call needed.
It publishes at least one independent security attestation (such as a SOC 2 report or an ISO 27001 certificate).
It shipped a public release in the last 30 days.
